items.claim: Around 1389 Bishop Pierre d'Arcis wrote to Pope Clement VII that an artist had admitted painting the cloth; the pope allowed it to be shown only as a representation.

sources.title: Shroud of Turin
sources.note: Lirey (1350s); the d'Arcis memorandum; Chambéry fire 1532; Turin since 1578; Secondo Pia 1898; STURP 1978; the 1988 carbon dating; later studies.

items.claim: A 2025 3D study by Cicero Moraes found a low relief matches the image better than a body; the International Center of Sindonology disputes it.

sources.title: Shroud of Turin image came from a sculpture, 3D study suggests (2025)
sources.note: Cicero Moraes, Archaeometry 2025: a low relief fits better.

sources.title: Shroud of Turin center disputes new study (2025)
sources.note: The International Center of Sindonology's reply.
